content_sections.heading: About NBPGR
content_sections.text: ICAR-National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources is an ICAR institute at Pusa Campus, New Delhi – 110 012. These two posts serve the ICAR-CRP Genomics project "Genomics of black pepper, green cardamom and fenugreek for relating genes to traits of economic importance".

content_sections.heading: NBPGR Young Professional-II Vacancy Details 2026
content_sections.text: Pay may be released as per the satisfaction of the Principal Investigator (PI) and the availability of funds from the funding agency. FREEJOBALERT DAILY QUIZ Preparing for Govt Exams? Test Yourself! 25 Questions · 20 Minutes · Instant Score Take Today's Free Quiz →

content_sections.heading: NBPGR Young Professional-II Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: Post-Graduation in Agricultural Sciences/ Bioinformatics/ Biotechnology/ Life Sciences/ Botany/ Genetics. Each degree and diploma should be from a UGC recognized university. Minimum two years' experience in the relevant area of research. Only candidates who hold the essential qualification will be considered for the interview. Post 1: Experience of wet lab work in Next Generation Sequencing, transcriptomics, real time PCR and routine molecular biology techniques. Post 2: Knowledge of programming in Linux/R, and proficiency in using licensed and open source software for NGS data analyses. Check the official notification for the full eligibility of each post before attending.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Screening of documents brought to the walk-in. Eligible candidates face an in-person interview before the Selection Committee at NBPGR, Pusa Campus, New Delhi. The decision of the Director of the institute is final and binding in all respects. No TA/DA is paid for attending the interview.

content_sections.heading: Service Conditions
content_sections.text: Duration: 3 years. The first engagement is for one year. It can be extended for two more years on a yearly basis, depending entirely on satisfactory performance. The post is purely temporary and co-terminus with the project. There is no claim to regularisation or absorption in ICAR/NBPGR. The Director may end the contract even before the project is completed, and no appeal will be entertained. Any dispute falls under the jurisdiction of New Delhi only.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for NBPGR Young Professional-II Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Download the official notification and print the application format in Annexure I. Fill in the post applied for (serial number and post name), personal details, Aadhar number, education from 10th onwards, experience, research publications with NAAS ratings, and NOC status. Paste a passport size photograph and sign the declaration. Report at ICAR-NBPGR New Building, Pusa Campus, New Delhi 110012 on 27 November 2026 at 10.00 AM. Hand in the filled form with the documents below at the time of interview. Filled application form as per Annexure I, with one passport size photograph Self-attested copies of all relevant certificates and marksheets from matriculation onwards Original certificates and marksheets, plus an identity proof, for verification Copy of Aadhar card No Objection Certificate from the present employer, if employed The form asks for copies of the original degrees and marksheets instead of provisional certificates. Candidature can be cancelled at any stage if any information is found incorrect or any fact is concealed.

faq.question: Q1. How many Young Professional-II posts are there at NBPGR?
faq.answer: There are two posts, both under the ICAR-CRP Genomics project on black pepper, green cardamom and fenugreek.

faq.question: Q2. When and where is the walk-in interview?
faq.answer: It is on 27 November 2026 at 10.00 AM in the ICAR-NBPGR New Building, Pusa Campus, New Delhi.

faq.question: Q3. What is the monthly pay for YP-II?
faq.answer: The pay is Rs 42,000 per month, consolidated.

faq.question: Q4. What qualification is needed?
faq.answer: A post-graduation in agricultural sciences, bioinformatics, biotechnology, life sciences, botany or genetics from a UGC recognized university, plus at least two years' research experience in the relevant area.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit and relaxation?
faq.answer: Candidates must be 21 to 45 years old as on the date of advertisement. The upper limit is relaxed by 5 years for women and SC/ST candidates and by 10 years for PwD candidates.

faq.question: Q6. What skills give an edge for each post?
faq.answer: Post 1 prefers wet lab work in NGS, transcriptomics, real time PCR and molecular biology techniques. Post 2 prefers Linux/R programming and NGS data analysis software skills.

faq.question: Q7. How long is the engagement?
faq.answer: It is for 3 years: one year at first, then extended yearly for two more years based on satisfactory performance.

faq.question: Q8. Is TA/DA paid for attending the interview?
faq.answer: No, no TA/DA is paid for appearing in the interview.

faq.question: Q9. Do employed candidates need an NOC?
faq.answer: Yes, candidates who are currently employed should produce a No Objection Certificate from their present employer.
